A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPORTU and contain readable main text, tables, figures and appendices. Their shared benchmark, experiments and examples can be matched reliably despite substantial appendix reorganization. Conflicting sport descriptions create the specific uncertainty noted under E1.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on SPORTU, including accuracy, explanation scores, human ratings, multi-angle consistency and error analyses in Sections 4–5 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v3 retains original SPORTU evaluations and adds results for prompting strategies, additional models, multiple evaluators and text-question categories.

M1.justification: The proposed benchmark and its basic construction approach remain unchanged. The additional standard prompting strategies and evaluator models extend experimental comparisons; they do not introduce a proposed model, training objective or new reasoning algorithm.

E1.justification: Both retain 900 text questions, 1,701 videos, 12,048 video QA pairs and the same task families. However, v1 lists table tennis among the five text sports, whereas v3 lists basketball. Basketball already appears in v1 Figure 1, so the PDFs do not establish whether the underlying coverage changed or its description was corrected.

E2.justification: The four SPORTU-text models remain unchanged. SPORTU-video removes GPT-4V and adds ST-LLM and Qwen2-VL-72B in the reported QA, multi-angle and error comparisons. This updates a limited portion of the otherwise retained model suite.

E3.justification: Video evaluation expands from answer-then-rationale prompting to three strategies, adding answer-only and rationale-first conditions. GPT-4o-only explanation judging becomes four evaluators for text and three for video, with averaged scores. Text prompt templates also change substantively, especially zero-shot CoT; this establishes a reported protocol revision, not that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds a systematic prompting sensitivity study across models and difficulty levels, with contrasting outputs in Appendix H. It also adds a paired camera-angle case study and substantially expands diagnostic error cases in Appendix Q. The multi-angle consistency analysis and five-category error taxonomy already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Pearson correlation with human ratings already appears in v1. Additional evaluator scores and correlations extend the results without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial prompt-specific, evaluator-specific and text-category results, including Qwen2-VL-72B's 70.94% under answer-only prompting. Reported Llama3.1 zero-shot-CoT accuracy changes from 61.95% to 64.44%, and Gemini 1.5 Pro's hard answer-then-rationale accuracy changes from 53.53% to 43.53%. These are reported-value revisions, not established same-setting improvements. GPT-4V results and v1 Table 7's per-sport video breakdown disappear.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theorems, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations. The added X/Y/R prompting notation describes experimental strategies; the existing multi-angle consistency definitions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central benchmark contribution and claim that models struggle with sports reasoning remain. v3 adds a prominent claim about answer-only prompting outperforming rationale generation and identifies Qwen2-VL-72B as the overall video leader. Its abstract corrects the hard-task leader to GPT-4o, whose 57.84% was already reported in v1 Table 4, although v3's introduction still names Claude.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands explanations of failure mechanisms: erroneous rationales influencing answers, inadequate frame extraction and grounding, and failure to connect recognized movements with rules. Appendix Q supplies explicit reasons for individual error classifications. These additions go beyond v1's broader discussion of hallucination, question misunderstanding and camera-angle inconsistency.

D1.justification: v3 documents manual question categorization, replay-based extraction of camera views, Qwen2-VL-72B API access and more explicit prompt templates. It omits v1's statement that few-shot exemplars came from a development set. Hardware, frame budgets and dataset access are largely retained; the quality-control procedure is relocated rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for Qwen-VL, ST-LLM and multimodal chain-of-thought reasoning, and removes the GPT-4V system-card reference. The positioning against existing sports QA benchmarks remains substantially unchanged; the dataset comparison table is moved to Appendix A.

P1.justification: The document undergoes substantial structural reorganization: quality control moves into the main text, experimental setup is separated into models and prompting strategies, and the appendices become distinct thematic sections with a contents listing. The introduction and conclusion are rewritten, and duplicated abstract and introduction sentences are removed.

P2.justification: The main video accuracy table is redesigned around prompting strategies, explanation tables gain evaluator columns, and new breakdown tables are added. The correlation heatmap expands, prompt templates are reformatted, and many examples are redrawn with colored answer and error-explanation panels. Existing examples and the benchmark comparison table are also redistributed.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's single video prompting strategy and GPT-4o-only judging, v3 provides useful evidence about sensitivity to prompting and evaluator choice, supported by clearer diagnostic examples. The net gain is limited by removal of the per-sport video breakdown and reporting problems: Table 3 supports direct-answer dominance for only 6 of 14 models, tied with answer-then-rationale, while Table 8 contains inconsistent overall and subgroup accuracies. These issues limit the strength of the added interpretations.
